headline: Selecting Moisture-Resistant Basement Flooring: Luxury Vinyl Plank vs Carpet
articleBody:
Selecting the right flooring for a finished basement comes down to managing concrete moisture and everyday comfort. Basement slabs constantly release ground vapor, which limits how traditional flooring materials perform over time.

Comparing Your Options
Homeowners usually weigh luxury vinyl plank (LVP) against basement-rated carpet. Here is how they stack up in below-grade settings:

- Moisture resilience: Luxury vinyl plank is made from synthetic polymers that will not warp or rot from occasional dampness. Carpet fibers and padding, however, hold moisture. EPA guidance warns against carpeting in rooms with chronic dampness because trapped water quickly leads to persistent odors and mold growth.
- Subfloor preparation: LVP requires a flat, smooth slab; small dips or ridges will cause planks to click or separate over time. Carpet is forgiving over uneven concrete, but it still requires a dry surface to protect the pad beneath.
- Warmth and sound: Carpet provides superior thermal insulation and dampens footsteps. LVP feels cooler and harder underfoot unless you pair it with an approved subfloor underlayment or thermal break.
- Maintenance and replacement: LVP wipes clean after accidental spills and resists heavy traffic. When carpet padding gets soaked by a pipe leak or foundation seepage, the entire section often has to be torn out and discarded.
